cover.title: The Number That Moves The Fed
cover.label: CPI

lines.text: Wednesday's inflation number could push the Fed to raise rates again.
lines.say: Wednesday's inflation number could push the Fed to raise rates again.

lines.text: In August, prices were up 3.4% from a year earlier. Forecasts for September: about 3.6%.
lines.say: In August, prices were up three point four percent from a year earlier. Forecasts for September? About three point six.

lines.text: In 2026, inflation climbed from 2.4% in January to a 4.2% peak in May as gas prices soared.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-six, inflation climbed from two point four percent in January to a four point two percent peak in May, as gas prices soared.

lines.text: So on September 16, the Fed raised rates to 3.75%-4%, its first hike since 2023.
lines.say: So on September sixteenth, the Fed raised rates to three point seven five to four percent, its first hike since twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: Now the week ahead. Tuesday, October 13, big banks start reporting earnings.
lines.say: Now the week ahead. On Tuesday, October thirteenth, the big banks start reporting earnings.

lines.text: Wednesday at 8:30 AM Eastern, the September inflation report drops.
lines.say: Wednesday at eight thirty Eastern, the September inflation report drops.

lines.text: And on October 28, the Fed decides again.
lines.say: And on October twenty-eighth, the Fed decides again.

lines.text: Why care? Credit card and home equity rates usually move with the Fed's rate, and so do savings yields.
lines.say: Why care? Credit card and home equity rates usually move with the Fed's rate, and so do savings yields.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Wednesday's inflation report could push the Fed to hike
post.ig:
Wednesday's inflation number could push the Fed to raise rates again.
September CPI comes out Wed, Oct 14, 2026, at 8:30 AM ET. Forecasts point to about 3.6% a year, up from 3.4% in August.
Inflation peaked at 4.2% in May 2026 as gas prices soared. On Sept 16 the Fed raised rates to 3.75%-4%, its first hike since 2023.
Next Fed decision: Oct 28. Card, HELOC and savings rates usually move with the Fed's rate.
Sources: BLS, Federal Reserve, Reuters (Oct 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
